WHAT_A_NEXT_MoE_SPECIMEN_INHERITS: Per-EXPERT activation statistics beat pooled ones for any routed architecture. Pooled weighting made 1-bit WORSE (+1.9%/+1.0%) while per-expert made it BETTER (-7.1%/-10.3%) at identical bytes. This is a property of routing, not of Kimi-VL, and should transfer to every MoE in the lake (qwen3_moe x2, qwen3_vl_moe, lfm2_moe, granitemoehybrid x2, glm4_moe).

Perplexity ALONE will pass a model that cannot generate. q2-g128-experts scored ppl 4.085, only 41% above bf16, while emitting 87 consecutive identical tokens. Any capability gate needs a generation-coherence term, and n=1 generation is not enough - n=1 verdicts were overturned by n=8.

A capability gate must be calibrated against the SOURCE model measured on the same prompts. Without a bf16 arm every quantized config scores 0.50-0.75 on 4-gram repetition and they look mutually comparable; the reference is what supplies the scale.
Weight-space cosine is NOT a monotone proxy for capability. Per-expert calibration lowers cosine while improving perplexity. It survives only as a coarse cross-class pass/fail screen.

The magnitude-adequacy gate is BLIND to quantization failure: every arm scores 0.994-1.042 because affine fitting preserves magnitude by construction. It still catches 0.01*W, so keep it, but never use it as the capability proxy.
For the mean-|W| sign quantizer, cosine == magnitude ratio EXACTLY (proved and verified at delta 0.00e+00). Two gates, one number. Do not count them as independent evidence.
mx.quantize supports bits 2,3,4,5,6,8 and groups 32,64,128 ONLY. Any search grammar built on it floors around 2.19 EBPW, above a 1.0 target, so sub-bit work needs a hand-written class.

Decode is bandwidth-bound only near bf16 (56.5% of peak). Quantized configs run at 18-23% of peak, so below roughly q4 removing bytes buys no decode speed - the ceiling is per-token fixed cost. Expect the EBPW/TPS correlation to break at the same place on other specimens.
Measure TPS with >=6 warm repeats. Two repeats and one warmup under-reported decode by up to 35% here (q4: 98.24 vs 127.48) while preserving the ranking.
WHAT_A_NEXT_MoE_SPECIMEN_MUST_RE_MEASURE: The gate thresholds themselves - they are 1.25x/3x of THIS model's bf16 numbers.
Where the affine class stops passing. O003 breaks between q3 and q2; that boundary depends on expert width (1408x2048 here) and top-k (6 of 64) and cannot be assumed.
The bandwidth knee. It is a function of active bytes/token, which depends on top_k/n_experts and the dense fraction, all specimen-specific.
Whether MLA-style attention needs a custom sanitize patch to load at all (O003 did, for kv_b_proj).
Absolute EBPW of every class: they depend on the expert/non-expert byte split, 90.2% here.
NOT_YET_ATTACKED_on_this_specimen: Codebook / product quantization of expert weights.
Structured sparsity or pruning before binarisation.
Cross-layer or cross-expert weight sharing (killed in weight space per O003_PROV.json, untested under activation weighting).
Error-feedback / iterative refit (GPTQ-style) rather than one-shot fitting.
Any kernel for the sparse or binary forms - so no TPS exists for them.
